title: Axonal input predicts which task variables a mouse brain region encodes, beyond distance and shared probes, in IBL Brain-Wide Map (182 regions) and Steinmetz 2019 (57 regions) data
abstract: Question: does the mesoscale connectome set which task variables each mouse brain region encodes? Approach: for 182 IBL Brain-Wide Map regions and 5 variables (stimulus, choice, feedback, wheel speed, block prior), I regressed the published decoding score of each region and variable on the input-weighted mean score of the same variable in its source regions (Knox 2019 connection density). The model has region and variable fixed effects and controls for distance-weighted neighbours, probe co-recording and brain division. Inference used 1,000 permutations of wiring labels within divisions and a stricter null that shuffles inputs among sources at equal distance. Result: the pre-specified coefficient was +0.34 SD per SD (null means -0.07 and 0.00; p = 0.001 for both nulls). It stayed positive for other BWM analysis types, distance scales, weight forms, within- and between-division inputs and leave-one-variable-out fits. In an independent replication with my own decoders on Steinmetz et al. 2019 (57 regions, 4 variables), the coefficient was +0.37 (one-sided p = 0.004; distance-preserving null p = 0.001), and +0.59 for 39 regions with at least 2 sessions. The match held for stimulus, choice and feedback but not for wheel speed. Limitations: the evidence is correlational and region-level; shared third-party input or cell-type composition can also cause it; both tests use the same Knox anatomy; the distance-preserving null was added after the first result; one pre-specified log-weight variant was uninformative because it made the predictor collinear with the fixed effects.

display.caption: Variable specificity. After region-mean removal, correlation of each target variable (rows) with the input-weighted source encoding of each variable (columns). Diagonal values are in bold. Left: IBL BWM decoding scores, 182 regions. Right: Steinmetz 2019, my decoders, 57 regions. No controls are applied in this plot.

Observed wiring coefficient beta_in (orange line, full model with distance, co-recording and division controls) against 1,000 null coefficients: wiring labels shuffled within Cosmos divisions (blue), and inputs shuffled among sources in the same distance decile (green).
beta_in minus its permutation-null mean, with bars at +-1.96 null SD, for all IBL (blue) and Steinmetz (orange) models. The uninformative log10(W/min+1) variant is omitted (see README).
